# Why coding agents need visible coordination

> See which agent needs input, where it is editing, and what changed. Paneflow keeps that work visible while separating read-only access from terminal control.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/blog/philosophy-of-paneflow

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

When Claude Code edits a feature and Codex reviews it, you need to know which files they share, whether either agent is waiting for input, and what the implementation changed. Paneflow keeps their terminals and code review tools together in a native terminal multiplexer for coding agents. You can inspect the work and intervene while it is happening.

Visible coordination means keeping enough context to decide what happens next: answer an agent, wait for a test, correct a file, or stop a task. A status indicator helps you find the terminal that needs attention. The terminal output and code show you what that attention requires.

## See the task behind each terminal

A project tab can hold an agent, a test runner, and a dev server in separate panes. Several agents can share the tab too. Grouping those terminals lets you read a test failure beside the agent's explanation and take over a terminal when needed. Activity tracking depends on the integration available for each agent; a quiet terminal alone does not establish that a task succeeded.

The working directory matters as much as the pane. Two terminals in the same checkout edit the same files. That can suit an implementation agent and a reviewer that only reads. For independent edits, a separate branch and [Git worktree](/docs/worktrees) give each task its own working directory. The branches still need to be reviewed together when you integrate them.

## Review the changes behind the report

An agent's completion message tells you what it believes it did. **Changes** shows the active checkout's staged and unstaged changes and untracked files against `HEAD`. You can inspect the patch, then open a file in **Files** to read its context or make a correction beside the terminal.

This view covers local changes. Once they are committed, use the full branch diff to review the contribution, as the [Changes guide](/blog/diff-viewer) explains. Review also includes the checks required by the project and the combined result when several branches are involved. An idle agent, a completion report, and correct code are three different things.

## Share output with explicit permissions

An agent reviewing a change may need to read the implementation agent's test output. Paneflow's [read-only MCP bridge](/docs/scripting) exposes `list_panes`, `read_pane`, and `search_pane` for that purpose. It lets agents find panes and inspect their output without copying text between conversations. It cannot type, submit prompts, or control another pane. Terminal output remains data to examine, even when it contains text that looks like an instruction.

The CLI can send text when separately authorized. `paneflow send` requires scripting permission or **AI free access**, even to prefill text; pressing Enter through the CLI additionally requires `--submit`. You can give an agent access to another terminal's output without giving it control of that terminal.

## Return to work that is still running

Closing the interface does not have to end a task. Choosing **Keep sessions running** when quitting leaves the terminals and their processes in a separate local host. Reopening Paneflow reconnects to them while that host and the machine remain running.

Restarting an ended terminal starts a fresh shell. Resuming an agent conversation uses that agent's saved history. Neither operation restores a process after a machine restart or host crash. The [session persistence documentation](/docs/features) explains what each operation preserves, so you can tell whether you are returning to live work or starting again.

## Local execution has a precise meaning

Paneflow runs the terminals locally. Each agent connects to its own model provider, so local terminal execution does not mean every model request stays on your machine. Desktop telemetry is opt-in and excludes terminal contents, paths, and prompts. `PANEFLOW_NO_TELEMETRY=1` disables it regardless of configuration.

Paneflow is free software under [GPL-3.0-or-later](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/blob/v0.17.5/LICENSE). It provides ways to observe and control the work. Deciding whether a patch meets the task, whether its checks are sufficient, and which changes to integrate remains part of your review.
